# Synthetic .NET envelope fixtures

`FanAndLighting.zip` and `Screen.zip` are generated by the adjacent `Producer.cs`
with standard `System.Text.Json` default options and `ZipArchive`/Optimal.
The DTO property names, numeric MainType/ProfileTypes and LCDV2 SubType follow
source observation of L-Connect3 version2.1.28.0. All values and the text asset
are owned synthetic data; no vendor assembly/assets/profile or device is used.
The embedded profile is a small structural example, not a full vendor profile.
These files prove BCL container/serialization compatibility only. They do not
prove conversion, media validation, WPF/color serialization or real Windows
export/import interoperability. The deliberately non-media asset must not be
reported as validated media.

Generation used .NET runtime10.0.12 and C# compiler with `-noconfig -nostdlib`,
referencing that runtime's CoreLib, Runtime, Collections, Text.Json and
IO.Compression assemblies. The compiler output runs with a matching runtimeconfig.
A .NET SDK console project containing only Producer.cs can generate the same
DTO/ZIP contents by passing this directory as its sole command-line argument.
The fixture producer is not needed to run Cargo tests.

`Cooling.zip` is produced separately by `CoolingProducer.cs` with the same BCL
runtime/compiler settings. Its enum-keyed dictionary exercises the default
System.Text.Json symbolic property keys while Mode properties remain numeric.
It contains eight owned fan modes, three pump modes, an unrelated first-generation
record and one LCDV2 record at index1. Built-in parameters deliberately differ
between modes so replacing inactive data with Linux presets fails the tests.
The source metadata, profile values and two placeholder unconverted root fields
are synthetic. This is a cooling container/DTO fixture, not a complete vendor
controller export, Windows application run or proof of full-group import.
Compile each producer as its own console program; both define Main.

`Lighting.zip` is generated separately by `LightingProducer.cs` using the same
.NET10.0.12 compiler/runtime setup. It contains6/16 enum-keyed lighting profiles,
numeric selected IDs and six enum-keyed High/Low sensor settings per pump mode.
Parameters deliberately vary between modes and sources. Colors are owned RGB
integer arrays matching the observed converter output shape; no WPF/vendor
converter runs. It proves .NET dictionary/JSON/container compatibility, not a
Windows application export or qualified import. Compile this producer alone.

`Control.zip` combines the owned LCDV2 records from `Cooling.zip` (index1) and
`Lighting.zip` (index0), retaining the unrelated cooling record at index0. Run
`python3 ControlProducer.py` in this directory to regenerate it deterministically.
It exercises the full FanAndLighting import through CLI, native worker and desktop
FileChooser without proprietary assets. This is a synthetic container assembled
from .NET-produced DTO fixtures, not a genuine Windows application export.

`ScreenBanks.zip` is generated by `python3 ScreenBanksProducer.py`. It is an owned
Python structural DTO fixture with distinct runtime/editor documents, eight banks,
nullable/empty names, three galleries and flat placeholder uploads (including an
unused file and thumbnail). It is not a .NET-produced fixture or genuine export;
its deliberately undecodable payloads exercise CRC/digest inventory only. Tests
must continue to report media decoding and group import as unsupported.

The runtime RGB-array fixtures above do not establish WPF's default storage
representation. Profile/editor Export uses default serialization, unlike runtime
config generation with explicit RGB converters. `tests/support/wpf_color.rs`
emulates the public byte/linear channel/null ColorContext properties without
loading WPF; newer source-codec tests cover these objects, raw lighting history
and exact editor source preservation. ICC/profiled colors remain unsupported;
genuine Windows exports and actual WPF serialization/deserialization are separate
qualification. The original RGB fixtures remain useful compatibility vectors.

`ScreenImage.png` is a two-pixel RGBA image generated deterministically by
`python3 ScreenImageProducer.py` using struct/zlib only. Its literal colors/alpha
exercise verified ZIP→normalizer ingestion. JPEG coverage encodes this owned image
through the existing image pipeline. No vendor media or real capture is used.
